source_text: Atra-hasis, Sippar Tablet III with synoptic motivation passages
approx_date: Composition date not independently verified in this revision
survivor: Atrahasis; his family is brought aboard
flood_decreed_by: The great Anunnaki decide together on oath; Enlil is blamed for bringing the flood
warned_by: Enki, addressing the reed wall and instructing Atrahasis
cause: Human multiplication and noise provoke successive divine attempts to reduce the population; the sequence escalates to the flood
vessel: A roofed boat strengthened with bitumen; its door is closed with bitumen
aftermath: Sacrifice; Enki addresses Nintu, followed by provisions for women who cannot bear, infant deaths and priestly restrictions on childbirth
inspected_scope: SEAL III C1 (+) C2, displayed translation i–viii; I 351–363; II A 1–20, E 56–78, G 16–97 and H 1–28
survivor_references: SEAL edition credited to Nathan Wasserman, 8 September 2020; indexing/commentary Yulia Tulaikova, 1 July 2021. Bibliography identifies Wasserman 2020, pp. 19–37, and Lambert/Millard 1969: C2 i 11′–24′; C1 ii 40″–52″; vi 5–19 (https://seal.huji.ac.il/node/1517?tid=80)

flood_decreed_by_note: The collective decision is recalled after the flood. This does not turn a later blame statement into a separately preserved pre-flood council scene.
warned_by_references: SEAL edition credited to Nathan Wasserman, 8 September 2020; indexing/commentary Yulia Tulaikova, 1 July 2021. Bibliography identifies Wasserman 2020, pp. 19–37, and Lambert/Millard 1969: C2 i 13′–24′; C1 i 36′–38′; vi 11–19 (https://seal.huji.ac.il/node/1517?tid=80)
warned_by_note: The speaker name at i 15′ is restored; vi 13–15 explicitly identifies Enki with the disclosure.

Streck, SEAL edition, translation and commentary, revision 29 December 2024: I 351–363 (https://seal.huji.ac.il/index.php/node/1515) | SEAL synoptic edition; revision history credits Nathan Wasserman, 10–11 August 2026: A 1–20; E 60–78; G 27–49u; H 9–25 (https://seal.huji.ac.il/index.php/node/39732?tid=339) | SEAL edition credited to Nathan Wasserman, 8 September 2020; indexing/commentary Yulia Tulaikova, 1 July 2021. Bibliography identifies Wasserman 2020, pp. 19–37, and Lambert/Millard 1969: C1 iii 36′–43′ (https://seal.huji.ac.il/node/1517?tid=80)
cause_note: Narrative sequence summarized across the synoptic edition: the first noise complaint prompts disease, then deprivation of food and water. The explicit flood oath at II G 49q–u comes from Middle Babylonian X-MB. Tablet III retrospectively links the destruction decision to the people’s noise; the causal sequence is not a verbatim single-line explanation.
vessel_references: SEAL edition credited to Nathan Wasserman, 8 September 2020; indexing/commentary Yulia Tulaikova, 1 July 2021. Bibliography identifies Wasserman 2020, pp. 19–37, and Lambert/Millard 1969: C2 i 22′–26′; C1 i 29′–33′; ii 51″–54″ (https://seal.huji.ac.il/node/1517?tid=80)
vessel_note: The damaged dimensions are not reconstructed; a reed-worker’s participation does not establish an exclusively reed hull.
birds_released_references: SEAL edition credited to Nathan Wasserman, 8 September 2020; indexing/commentary Yulia Tulaikova, 1 July 2021. Bibliography identifies Wasserman 2020, pp. 19–37, and Lambert/Millard 1969: C1 ii 34″–35″; iv 24′–27′ and following gap; v 1–31″ (https://seal.huji.ac.il/node/1517?tid=80)
birds_released_note: Birds are loaded aboard, but no test-release scene survives in this witness’s displayed translation. The gap around the flood’s ending prevents an absence claim.
landing_place_references: SEAL edition credited to Nathan Wasserman, 8 September 2020; indexing/commentary Yulia Tulaikova, 1 July 2021. Bibliography identifies Wasserman 2020, pp. 19–37, and Lambert/Millard 1969: C1 iv 24′–27′ and following gap; v 1–31″ (https://seal.huji.ac.il/node/1517?tid=80)
landing_place_note: The transition from storm to sacrifice is substantially missing; no landing location is preserved in the inspected translation.
aftermath_references: SEAL edition credited to Nathan Wasserman, 8 September 2020; indexing/commentary Yulia Tulaikova, 1 July 2021. Bibliography identifies Wasserman 2020, pp. 19–37, and Lambert/Millard 1969: C1 v 30″–35″; vi 41′–51′; vii 1–11 (https://seal.huji.ac.il/node/1517?tid=80)
aftermath_note: Enlil calls for Enki and Nintu to confer; Enki’s name is restored in vi 45′. The preceding assignment of Death in vi 47′–49′ is substantially restored, so it is not presented as an unqualified preserved clause.
